I've come back to Battlefield 6 multiple times hoping that something would finally click, and somehow every return has left me more disappointed than the last. I was genuinely excited for this game. Unfortunately, I can confidently say that the best state I ever played Battlefield 6 in was the beta.

The gunplay is one of the biggest downgrades. During the beta, it actually felt pretty decent. Weapons had weight, firefights felt satisfying, and I came away optimistic about the direction they were taking. The full game somehow took that foundation and made it substantially worse. Now the gunplay feels far more like Call of Duty than Battlefield. Guns will feel like absolute laser beams for part of a match, and then suddenly the netcode decides you're firing blanks. Shots that look and feel like they should connect simply don't, and the inconsistency makes firefights frustrating rather than satisfying. Combine that with maps that often feel half-thought-out and sightlines that encourage snipers everywhere, and infantry combat quickly becomes exhausting. Snipers used to feel like a relatively small portion of the playerbase outside of maps specifically suited for them. Here, it feels like you're constantly being watched from six different zip codes.

Then there's dogfighting.

The golden standard of Battlefield dogfighting was stripped away, dragged into the street, and shot. What used to make Battlefield's air combat so much fun was the actual fight. Positioning, maneuvering, speed control, knowing when to disengage, reversing an advantage, and having prolonged battles between skilled pilots were what made getting into a jet exciting. Now? The time-to-kill can be around half a second. At that point, it's barely dogfighting. It's opportunism. Whoever happens to catch the other jet at the right angle first generally deletes them before an actual fight can develop. There's very little opportunity to outmaneuver somebody or turn a bad engagement around because you're dead before the fight even gets interesting. Worse, jets frequently end up camping the enemy spawn because apparently we needed to abandon another Battlefield concept that already worked perfectly well: the enemy's spawn is out of bounds.

Which brings me to the huge "Top Gun: Carrier Strike" update.

The concept is genuinely awesome. Fight for air superiority, capture control points containing salvo missiles, use those missiles to damage the enemy carrier, and eventually breach and board it. On paper, that sounds like exactly the kind of large-scale combined-arms insanity Battlefield should excel at. In practice, the match starts and people immediately rush the enemy aircraft carrier. Instead of fighting over the objectives and gradually earning the ability to attack the carrier, players can get onto the enemy carrier, destroy or steal vehicles, camp the spawn, and generally turn the entire thing into a miserable experience from practically the opening minutes of the match. And apparently this massive aircraft carrier has essentially no meaningful close-in air defense to prevent it. That is an especially wild design choice considering real aircraft carriers don't just sit around politely waiting for enemy aircraft to strafe their flight decks. Even setting gameplay balance aside, the real-world inspiration for these ships includes close-in weapon systems specifically intended to help defend the vessel against threats. Yet in a game mode literally centered around air superiority and attacking an aircraft carrier, apparently giving the carrier meaningful defenses against enemy aircraft was a bridge too far.

Then there's the UI, which may genuinely be the worst menu interface I've ever used in a Battlefield game.

Trying to navigate Battlefield 6's menus feels like I'm browsing an adware-infested version of Hulu while simultaneously trying to figure out how to join my friend. Things that should require one or two obvious clicks are buried beneath oversized tiles, menus, submenus, promotional panels, and an interface seemingly designed to make simple tasks as unintuitive as possible.

I wanted to like this game. I've repeatedly come back because I remember how much I enjoyed the beta and so many other Battlefields and keep hoping I'll find that experience again.

Battlefield 6: A Beautiful and Deeply Concerning Experience

AI DISCLAIMER: This review was written entirely by a human. No Artificial Intelligence was involved. Any evidence suggesting otherwise is purely coincidental and should be ignored.

Battlefield 6 is a game about many things.

War.

Strategy.

Teamwork.

Explosions.

Architecture.

And, apparently, the consequences of giving a group of emotionally unstable adults access to military equipment.

From the moment I entered the battlefield, I knew I was experiencing something special. The atmosphere immediately communicated an important message:

something has gone terribly wrong.

And I was having an excellent time.

The gameplay is exceptionally satisfying. Weapons feel powerful, movement feels responsive, and there is an almost therapeutic quality to watching a building collapse because somebody decided that walls were merely a suggestion.

The destruction deserves particular recognition.

Most games treat buildings as permanent structures.

Battlefield 6 disagrees.

Battlefield 6 looks at a perfectly functional building and asks:

“What if it wasn't?”

This is innovation.

The multiplayer experience is equally impressive. Teamwork is strongly encouraged, although the game also understands that sometimes your entire squad will completely ignore the objective and collectively run in the same direction for reasons that will never be explained.

This creates an authentic representation of human decision-making.

The classes also provide meaningful variety. Different roles encourage different approaches to combat, allowing players to contribute according to their preferred playstyle.

Or you can simply choose whatever has the coolest gun.

This is also strategy.

The sound design deserves special attention.

Everything is loud.

Extremely loud.

A bullet passes nearby: loud.

A vehicle explodes: loud.

A building collapses: very loud.

Someone fires a weapon approximately 600 metres away: somehow also loud.

It creates an incredibly immersive audio experience and has successfully convinced me that I should probably wear hearing protection while playing a video game.

The visuals are equally impressive. The environments feel detailed, the effects are spectacular, and the battlefield possesses an almost cinematic quality.

Except cinemas generally don't have someone parachuting onto a roof while firing a rocket launcher at a tank.

Which is probably why cinemas are inferior.

One of my favourite aspects is the sheer unpredictability.

You can begin a match with a clear objective.

You can carefully plan your route.

You can coordinate with your squad.

And then a tank appears from somewhere it absolutely should not be able to appear from.

You die.

You respawn.

You do it again.

This is the circle of life.

Battlefield 6 also creates some genuinely memorable moments.

Sometimes you perform an incredible play and feel like a military genius.

Sometimes you accidentally throw a grenade directly into your own team's feet.

Both experiences are equally valuable.

One builds confidence.

The other builds character.

And this, ultimately, is what makes Battlefield 6 so compelling.

It doesn't simply ask you to win.

It asks you to participate in the chaos.

You are not always the hero.

You are not always the best player.

Sometimes you are simply a man standing in a field wondering why there is a helicopter approaching at approximately 900 kilometres per hour.

And that is beautiful.

In conclusion, Battlefield 6 is an explosive, chaotic, visually impressive and deeply entertaining multiplayer experience.

It has destruction.

It has teamwork.

It has vehicles.

It has guns.

It has people screaming.

It has buildings that used to exist.

What more could a person reasonably request from a video game?

Battlefield 6 has genuinely good gunplay. It's twitchy and fast-paced, but it's an arcade shooter, and when you're actually fighting other players it can still be a lot of fun.

Unfortunately, BF6 also feels like a perfect example of the state of modern AAA gaming. It no longer feels like the goal is simply to make an amazing game that people want to buy and play. The game itself has become a platform designed to hold your attention, advertise things to you and extract more money after you've already paid for it.

The Netflix-style menus sum this up perfectly. Giant tiles, cosmetics, bundles, promotions and layers of flashy presentation dominate an interface that should simply help me get into a Battlefield match. The presentation increasingly feels built around engagement and monetisation rather than the game itself.

That's what makes me miss the older Battlefield games. They weren't perfect, but they felt like games first and products second. The excitement came from destruction, huge battles, vehicles, teamwork and completely unscripted Battlefield moments. The menus didn't need to constantly remind you that there was something else you could buy.

Many of the developers who helped establish what Battlefield was have since moved on to other projects, and personally I find it telling that some of those games seem more interested in experimenting and simply being fun. Meanwhile Battlefield feels increasingly shaped by the corporate reality surrounding modern AAA development.

And I don't think Battlefield is alone. It's part of a wider industry that has realised there's potentially more money in turning games into ongoing storefronts than simply selling people a great game. Battle passes, cosmetics, engagement systems and carefully designed storefronts aren't extras anymore — they're increasingly part of the foundation the game is built around.

Underneath all of this, BF6 still has good gunplay. But then you have horrible netcode, infantry being farmed by vehicles and matches increasingly populated by bots.

I don't hate Battlefield 6. I hate what it represents.

I miss when Battlefield seemed more interested in giving me an unforgettable battle than selling me the next thing.

[h1] Battlefield 6 [/h1]
[i] More like Ratfield 6 amiright [/i]

[h3] Multiplayer [/h3]
As a lifelong boomer and enjoyer of battlefield since the days of the still unbeaten Bad Company 2 i was very apprehensive(Especially after the trash that is 2042) when this game was announced promising a return to boots on the ground and classic all out warfare. I like many others had come to the conclusion that DICE no longer knew how to(Self Admitted) make a good battlefield shooter. I am happy to report that i was mostly wrong and this new breed of battlefield is closer to what we always wanted yet somehow still misses the mark with too small map design, weapon balance and controller(Derogatory) recoil reduction that makes fights feel inconsistent.

The greatest sin apart from the horrific progression system seeing you play 20 hours to get 1 max lvl gun is most definitely how small the maps feel making combat engagements feel random and allowing vehicles to sometimes be too oppressive if your team is awful which lets face it they always are lol. The lack of any naval warfare at launch coming only 4 seasons too late is also an appalling decision.

The player base is also sometimes infuriating in the way they play. Teams refuse to play the objective, medics refuse to play the role at all, vehicle hoggers wait at spawn all game and contribute 1 kill(themselves) when they eventually slam into a light pole taking with them any poor soul that spawned on them and worst of all the dreaded COD player who cant imagine playing a shooter not high on a tub of G-Fuel sliding around every corner.

[i] TLDR [/i]
Its a great shooter at heart but lacks a lot of the heart that core battlefield players loved. This is a very large step in the right direction and hopefully they nail it on the next one.

[h3] RedSec [/h3]
What i consider the real meat of the game is surprisingly the Battle Royale(Ranked) which provides a great sense of accomplishment and tension as you cut your way through countless enemy teams all ready to take your life to come out on top. I might be biased here as i play often with a core group of friends and never touch the solo experience but this is bar none the best BR on the market as of right now(2026) Modern Warfare 2019 still being my favorite all time.

This like the main game is also deeply flawed in implementation at times like the RNG loadout missions that sometimes see you kitted out within minutes to never getting a single gun and having to shoot peas at your enemies. The gun balance is also awful as DICE seems incapable of shaking up the META making it so that only about 3 guns are ever worth using.

There is also a lack of map variety as in none with only one map out as of mid season 4. The map is serviceable but has very bad transitionary periods where it feels like there is not enough cover at times and most circles that end in the downtown area turn into a whoever is already in the final circle game wins ending.

[i] TLDR [/i]
Great mode let down by long term support and gun balance to keep it fresh. Fun time if you can get a good group of friends to mess around with. Unfortunately you have to play with the painfully slow multiplayer progression system to get good loadouts if you have any hope of winning.

[h3] Gameplay [/h3]
[b] BLOOM WHY? [/b]
Gunplay in this game is very good if only it wasn't for the decision to implement a completely random dispersion of your bullets that often don't actually shoot where you are aiming causing you to question whether you got bloomed, shot or hacked to death. The gunfights are very inconsistent at times and yes even snipers have this for some insane reason. Other than that the mix of vehicles, infantry and gadgets gives the game a nice mix of things to do and systems to engage with that make every match different.

[h3] Graphics [/h3]
Battlefield has always looked good even when it was a bit more cartoony like Bad Company. This game is no different with excellent looking gun models and terrain like most FROSTBITE ENGINE games. Of course any real gamer will immediately lower it all to low to get better fps and visibility.

[h3] Performance [/h3]
The game runs very well and is devoid of any hitches or frame drops during gameplay that would affect your gunfights. Keep in mind that me and my friends all have good hardware so your millage may vary.

[h3] Score [/h3]

-Return to boots on the ground
-Fun attack and defend loop
-Great Ranked Mode

[b] Cons [/b]
-Progression System is awful
-Bloom makes gunfight inconsistent
-Lack of support from DICE in areas like RedSec and gun balance

[b] Mixed [/b]

Battlefield 1 was way better with the themes, vibes, game modes, and overall immersion. This is also a good game but we do need to bring back battlefield 1 vibes, seriousness, grand scale, and operations mode.

The Good:
At launch, it felt like the savior of the franchise. It dropped the cringey specialists from 2042, brought back a grounded military setting, and nailed the core Class System. The initial betas and early weeks delivered incredible destruction, tight gunplay, and the classic Battlefield 4 sandbox vibe everyone had been begging for.

The Bad:
It only took a few updates for EA to completely butcher the game's momentum and ruin the good faith.

Mode Removal & Gutted Content: They actively butchered their own player base by pulling core game modes like Rush out of rotation to force everyone into their free-to-play Battle Royale.

Corporate Live-Service Pivot: The game shifted hard from a tactical, destruction-heavy sandbox into an aggressive microtransaction storefront. They flooded a full-priced $70 game with battle pass pop-ups, overly vibrant cosmetics, and grindy challenges.

Map Design & Server Issues: Instead of giving us massive, open, vehicle-heavy maps at launch, we got cramped layouts with poor flow. Throw in persistent hit-registration issues and the total lack of community-hosted persistent servers, and the classic server-browser ecosystem is completely gone.

Verdict:
It is heartbreaking because the raw foundation of a legendary Battlefield was right there. But EA once again proved they would rather kill a promising shooter with aggressive monetization, live-service bloat, and terrible playlist decisions than just let a great game be great. Stick to BF4.

- 32GB ddr4 3200MHz
- game on M2 SSD
- 3440x1440 165hz screen

The avg fps i get is 70-80 fps with frequent drops to 30-40 fps and drops to even 10 fps when near collapsing buildings, explosions, molotovs, smokes (so half the game).
The worst thing is that i play on MINIMAL settings - literally everything turned all the way down, no eyecandy options, no better effects, no better textures. IMO if you make such a sacrifice of graphics to get better fps (especially on a good hardware), you  should easily be able to saturate your monitor refreshrate.

Noteworthy is the fact that with such low settings, the jets and helicopters in the game look atrocious - the propellers stop spinning or do one revolution every couple of seconds, the jets kinda teleport around (this is not internet problems nor packet loss issue- my connection is suitable and i have tested this), so shooting them without aimlock guided missles is out of the question.

The gameplay, maps, flow of the game, weapon customization and selection are just so bad that i cannot believe this is supposed to be a full game - it rather feels like early alpha.

You can see that the publisher only cares about miliking you out of the money while letting the game and community ROT - massive amount of bugs, exploits not patched (In carrier strike mode, right from the start you can go to enemy carrier and spawncamp (it is not out of bounds area for any team) and  even better - you  can straight up end the match in first 5 minutes of the game by just attacking the carrier with vehicles (most notable is the jet minigun) - it will eat through the carrier health - no need to capture the points, no need to arm the explosives inside the enemy carrier - just two semi-good jets is all you need.

Not recommended to anyone who hopes for BF4 / BF play4free / BF Heroes / BF1 experience.

I bought this on sale, I would not buy it in the state it was in at launch last year.  It did not even feel like a Battlefield game.   After several beta weekends and free weeks, there is finally the Naval update.  

They brought back the gunboats (although they are a little different) from Battlefield 4, and island maps.   The new map Tsuru Reef is an excellent looking map, which feels like they at times put homages in there to other classic Battlefield maps.

They brought back Wake Island again for 2026,  So it is a full circle moment in ways. First seeing Wake Island  on Battlefield 1942 back in 2002 oh so many years ago.   To me, this Wake Island feels like Kharg Island 2.0 going back to Battlefield 3 2011.  It just has that feel for some reason.   Now with the gun boats.

The gunboats have added torpedoes,  and big booming battleship like canons on the back.  While this stuff is cool I would have prefered they left the DV-15 and RCB-90 alone honestly.

TTK - This has been an issue the forum complained about since launch, comparing the guns to laser beams with no recoil, and that as soon as you see someone you are probably gonna lose.      Coming from MW4 Beta, TTK currently (because they can always patch this) feels worse imo than COD.

Time of dominion (vehicles)  - Vehicles do not seem to "last" quite as long anymore.   But it is a Battlefield game, huge sandbox, multiple vehicles now land and sea and air.    

Two person fighter jets added something to it.            It actually fit with the current Top Guin theme.    

So Battlefield is now many games in one, it is air combat or ace combat for fighter jets, it is Hydro Thunder when you get boats out there jumoing waves and things.  And starting in Battlefield 3, Battlefield  proved that it could do Call Of Duty as well, with close quarters fast and highly detailed combat.

Some even calling this an outright Call Of Duty clone in its early days last year.     While I appreciate the chance to have those type of maps here and there.   I would rather see just Battlefield material if I am going to play Battlefield.

One of the main new features of this Battlefield is the ability to pull a downed teammate out of danger to revive them.   It adds an interesting mechanic to it all.

I predict - there will be a Battlefield 7, and it will be a PERFECTED Battlefield 6.    And perhaps more Naval and water based.  This will follow history of Battlefield 3 to Battlefield 4.   Kind of a Windows Vista VS Windows 7 thing..                   Maybe, we might even see once again player controllable aircraft carriers, submarines, and destroyers.    This would be a TRUE full circle back to Battlefield 1942 if that is the case.

I was surprised when they pulled the gun boats and water out like it was a Tueday, I did not expect that.   I have said before that I thought the water gave Battlefield 4 its longevity and replayability.  

And speaking of water, EA and Dice prove yet again that they have some of the best looking and feeling video game water out there.   Tsuru Reef and the crystal clear waters looked as pristine as Lost Islands on Battlefield 4.

Boat capsizing,  - this is new to this game.  The boat flipping all the way under allowing the player to see the under water world for a bit.  It was a surreal experience hahaha.  

Now all they need is some fabled "rogue" waves...                They could do a Bermuda Triangle map.  Its ALL water,  2 opposing carriers so a carrier strike map.       Maybe add where air craft could attack the carriers so that the Carriers could be "sinkable" like on 1942, this might be a good segway back to player controllable aircraft carriers for Battlefield 7...hint hint
